name: Software Delivery & Operations
description: Software delivery and operations connect changes in source code with the running services people use. This field brings together automated pipelines, workload management, monitoring, logs, and the protection of operational credentials.

seo.title: Software Delivery & Operations in Iran | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: Understand software pipelines, containers, monitoring, logs, and secrets, with clear distinctions between technical capabilities and verified Iranian adoption.

content.heading: From source code to a working service
content.content:
A software product has an operational life beyond the moment its code is written. Changes must be assembled, checked, delivered, and observed after release. Continuous integration and continuous delivery, usually abbreviated CI/CD, organize part of that journey into repeatable automated work. GitLab's documentation describes pipelines whose jobs can build applications, run tests, and deploy code. These are capabilities of the tooling; they do not establish how widely Iranian organizations use it. [s1]

This distinction matters when exploring Iran's technology businesses. A product demonstration can establish that a pipeline runs, while a claim about national adoption requires evidence from organizations or a representative survey. The sources inspected for this page support an explanation of the infrastructure, rather than a ranking of Iranian operators or an estimate of their market size.

content.heading: Different tools answer different questions
content.content:
Pipeline tools organize work around a change: what should run, in what order, and under which conditions? GitLab Runner supplies the execution side, receiving jobs and reporting their results. A repository server and the machines executing its jobs therefore have different responsibilities, even when one organization operates both. [s1][s2]

Container management addresses the running application. Kubernetes coordinates containerized workloads through declared configurations and automation. It does not replace every surrounding system: its overview explicitly distinguishes orchestration from building source code, prescribing a complete monitoring stack, or providing every application-level service. A release pipeline and a workload platform are complementary layers. [s3]

Monitoring asks whether a service is behaving acceptably. Google's site reliability engineering guidance distinguishes measurements taken inside a system from checks of its externally visible behavior. It emphasizes latency, traffic, errors, and saturation as useful signals. Logs supply event detail that can help explain a symptom, but collecting more records is not the same as establishing that users can complete a task. [s4]

content.title: A simplified delivery and feedback loop
content.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Source change"] -->|"Triggers configured work"| B["Pipeline jobs"]
  B -->|"Execute on"| C["Runner infrastructure"]
  C -->|"Produces"| D["Build output"]
  D -->|"Deployment job delivers"| E["Running service"]
  E -->|"Exposes behavior"| F["Monitoring and logs"]
  F -->|"Informs investigation"| A
```
content.summary: This editorial synthesis shows how automated execution and operational feedback can connect. It is a conceptual workflow, not a documented architecture of an Iranian organization or a claim that every deployment follows this sequence.

content.heading: Automation creates responsibilities
content.content:
Delivery infrastructure handles powerful permissions. GitLab warns that runners execute repository-defined code and can expose their hosts, other projects, or credentials if isolation is inadequate. The security boundary therefore extends beyond the application being built to the build environment itself. [s5]

Secrets management is another separate discipline. Kubernetes provides Secret objects for confidential values, but base64 encoding is not encryption. Its guidance calls for encryption at rest and restricted access. Merely placing a password in a platform's designated object does not demonstrate that the surrounding permissions and storage are secure. [s6]

Together, these distinctions explain the branches of this guide: pipelines automate change; containers organize execution; monitoring and logs support understanding; secrets management protects access; and DevOps services help organizations integrate those responsibilities. They also provide concrete subjects for assessing a service provider: demonstrable execution, understandable failure handling, controlled credentials, and evidence of operating the resulting system. These are evaluation questions derived from the documented responsibilities, rather than verified claims about any Iranian supplier. [s1][s3][s4][s5][s6]

name: GitLab & CI/CD Tools
description: GitLab CI/CD turns configured development tasks into automated jobs executed by runners. Understanding its role in Iran requires separating the software's technical capabilities from product-specific access policies and evidence of local use.

seo.title: GitLab & CI/CD Tools in Iran | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: How GitLab pipelines, runners, and build artifacts work, and why technical availability and Iran-specific service policies require separate evidence.

content.heading: Making development work repeatable
content.content:
Continuous integration brings automated checks into the process of combining code changes. The related delivery workflow prepares or deploys the resulting application. In GitLab, a pipeline configuration normally lives in a repository file named `.gitlab-ci.yml`; it describes jobs, stages, and execution conditions. Keeping those instructions alongside the application makes the automation part of the project's recorded changes. [s1]

A pipeline is a coordinated set of tasks, not an assurance that the application is correct. GitLab supports triggers including pushes, merge requests, schedules, and manual actions. Stages ordinarily proceed in sequence, while jobs within a stage can execute in parallel. A failed job usually prevents later stages from proceeding, although configured rules can alter that behavior. The checks selected by the project determine what a successful result establishes. [s2]

content.heading: Who executes a job, and what survives it?
content.content:
GitLab Runner executes the work on computing infrastructure and returns the result to GitLab. This separates pipeline coordination from the capacity that performs compilation, tests, or deployment. Administrators supplying that capacity must manage the runner infrastructure as an operational system in its own right. [s3]

Outputs also have distinct purposes. Job artifacts retain files associated with a pipeline, such as a compiled build or test report. Later jobs can retrieve those files. GitLab distinguishes these artifacts from caches, which accelerate work and should be safe to lose, and from package registries intended for versioned outputs used beyond a single pipeline. Container images belong in a container registry. These distinctions help explain why retaining source code alone is not equivalent to retaining a usable release. [s4]

The execution environment is a security boundary. GitLab's runner guidance warns that repository-defined jobs can compromise shared, persistent infrastructure and expose credentials. Privileged container execution can grant extensive host access. A runner's location therefore says little about its isolation unless the execution permissions are also understood. [s5]

content.heading: Iran: distinguish products, editions, and policies
content.content:
Access restrictions should be attributed to the specific supplier and product. The GitLab trade-compliance page inspected for this draft distinguishes Community Edition from Enterprise Edition, related technology, and services. It describes Community Edition as publicly available and outside the US Export Administration Regulations, while listing Iran among destinations restricted for the software covered by its stated export conditions. This is GitLab's description of its policy, not a determination that a particular transaction is permitted. [s6]

GitHub must be considered separately. Its trade-controls documentation says it obtained a US Office of Foreign Assets Control license to restore cloud services to developers in Iran. That statement cannot be transferred to GitLab or another vendor. Nor does either policy page demonstrate that a specific account, subscription, runner, or network path works in practice. [s7]

For this Iranian guide, the defensible conclusion is limited: pipeline architecture can be explained from primary documentation, while local implementation and access require additional evidence. No claim about GitLab's Iranian market share or the prevalence of self-hosting is supported by this source set.

name: Kubernetes & Container Management
description: Kubernetes manages containerized applications by coordinating workloads across a cluster of machines. Its architecture separates decisions about desired application state from the node-level work of running containers.

seo.title: Kubernetes & Container Management in Iran | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: Explore Kubernetes clusters, Pods, controlled rollouts, and security responsibilities, with explicit limits on evidence about Iranian adoption.

content.heading: Packaging an application and coordinating its execution
content.content:
Containers package applications with their runtime dependencies. Kubernetes supplies a platform for coordinating containerized workloads rather than requiring an operator to manage each running instance individually. Its central idea is declarative configuration: an operator describes a desired arrangement, and the system works toward that state. This does not make Kubernetes a complete application platform or remove the need for surrounding operational systems. [s1]

The distinction between packaging and orchestration is useful when reading descriptions of Iranian cloud services. A service that can run a container has not thereby demonstrated a particular Kubernetes architecture, managed-service responsibility model, or reliability outcome. Those require evidence about the actual offering. This page explains the underlying technology without attributing unverified capabilities to local providers.

content.heading: Inside a cluster
content.content:
A cluster separates control-plane functions from worker-node functions. The API server exposes the Kubernetes interface; etcd stores API-server data; the scheduler assigns unscheduled Pods to suitable nodes; and controllers implement the system's reconciliation behavior. On a node, the kubelet helps ensure that the specified Pods and their containers run, using a container runtime. A Pod is Kubernetes' smallest deployable workload unit. [s2][s3]

These components have different operational roles. Scheduling a workload is distinct from executing its containers, and retaining cluster configuration is distinct from preserving application data. The architecture therefore explains why a working application endpoint alone cannot establish the health or recoverability of every underlying component. That is an operational inference from the documented division of responsibilities. [s2]

content.title: How a Deployment becomes running application instances
content.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Operator"] -->|"Submits desired configuration"| B["Kubernetes API"]
  B -->|"Exposes Deployment state"| C["Deployment controller"]
  C -->|"Manages"| D["ReplicaSet"]
  D -->|"Maintains desired Pod count"| E["Pods"]
  F["Scheduler"] -->|"Assigns to suitable nodes"| E
  G["Node kubelet and runtime"] -->|"Run specified containers"| E
```
content.summary: The arrows distinguish configuration, controller ownership, scheduling, and execution. This is a simplified explanation of documented Kubernetes behavior, not a diagram of an Iranian provider's infrastructure.

content.heading: Controlled change still needs operational judgment
content.content:
A Deployment manages a set of Pods, commonly for an application that does not maintain state. Updating its Pod template creates a new ReplicaSet and allows a controlled transition between revisions. Kubernetes also provides rollout status and rollback mechanisms. A completed rollout establishes defined workload conditions; it does not independently verify every business function of the application. [s4]

Confidential configuration needs separate attention. Kubernetes Secrets can hold passwords, tokens, and keys, but their values are encoded rather than automatically encrypted in storage. The project recommends encryption at rest and narrowly granted access. Its guidance also explains that permission to create a Pod using a Secret can expose the Secret indirectly. Security therefore depends on effective permissions as well as object names. [s5]

content.heading: Persian documentation and the limits of local evidence
content.content:
The Kubernetes project provides a Persian-language documentation portal, with translated material and links to English sections. This is a concrete language-access resource, but its existence does not measure Iranian deployment numbers or demonstrate that every technical section is translated. [s6]

For an Iran-focused account, the next evidentiary step is documented implementation: who operates the control plane, which responsibilities remain with customers, and what independent evidence establishes service behavior. Until those details are verified, national adoption rates, provider comparisons, and claims of regional leadership would go beyond this source set.
